newsitem.title: CHINA: HK STOCKS SEEN EASING ON WALL STREET WEAKNESS.
newsitem.headline: HK STOCKS SEEN EASING ON WALL STREET WEAKNESS.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks are seen moving lower on Monday following a plunge in U.S. stock and bond markets on Friday on renewed fears of an interest rate rise, brokers said.

"After Friday's Wall Street fall, Hong Kong stocks are likely to open lower with the Hang Seng Index testing the low of 16,200 level," said Ricky Tam, senior research analyst at Delta Asia Securities.
The Dow industrials dived 156.78 points, or 1.91 percent, to 8,031.22 amid fears of rising interest rates fuelled by the latest set of strong U.S. economic figures.
The U.S. 30-year bond closed down 1-14/32 points to yield 6.64 percent.

"The market will take the high bond yields as an excuse to take profits after the steep rise in Hong Kong stocks last week, and interest rate-sensitive counters such as properties are likely to see heavy selling pressure," said Peter So, deputy head of research at Schroder Securities.
But sentiment remained positive and investors were waiting to buy at dips, he said.
The Hang Seng Index closed 25.73 points, or 0.15 percent, lower on Friday at 16,647.54 and the Hang Seng London Reference Index later lost 159.93 points, or 0.96 percent, to 16,487.61.
